cohort: The study included 448 registered cat breeders from 29 countries who provided data on 853 litters and 3560 live-born kittens from 45 pedigree cat breeds born in 2019.
finding: The incidence of dystocia requiring veterinary intervention was 14.9%, influenced by queen's age, gestation length, and litter size, and kitten mortality up to 12 weeks varied by breed and was affected by the requirement for Caesarean section and birth defects.
mod_finding: Caesarean section was required for 10.7% of litters and was identified as a factor affecting kitten mortality.
gest_age: Gestation length was measured, with a longer gestation period increasing the risk of dystocia.
